messages.content: {"task": "Extract four compact participation claims for three lexemes, using only the excerpts. Treat these as construction-specific draft records. For dependent few preserve both target selection and restrictions within its own phrase. For independent few preserve number/count and permitted dependents. For mine preserve the distinct bearers of possessor person and NP agreement. For some as a degree modifier of an adjective, return not_stated if the excerpts do not establish the use. Keep each conditions string under 70 words. Supply source IDs; unknown claims must have empty source_ids and empty conditions. List only forms supported by the excerpts. Do not invent facts or references. Do not answer from background grammatical knowledge.", "sources": [{"id": "S01", "locator": "determinatives-as-nouns.tex:247", "text": "\\textit{CGEL}'s treatment of \\mention{my} supplies a precedent for a restricted noun form \\citep[470--471]{huddleston2002}. Dependent \\mention{my} and independent \\mention{mine} belong to one pronoun paradigm. \\mention{My} remains a noun even though, in the ordinary NP construction, it requires a following nominal. The articles lack an independent argument form; their positive evidence is integration into determinative, and their nounhood depends on the category-level argument."}, {"id": "S03", "locator": "determinatives-as-nouns.tex:529", "text": "The genitive's person identifies the possessor; the independent NP's agreement reflects the possessed entity or entities. Compare constructed \\mention{Mine is ready} (\\enquote*{my contribution}) and \\mention{Mine are ready} (\\enquote*{my slides}). Ordinary Head therefore needs a constructional agreement condition. This extension isn't counted as a gain from determinative membership within Noun."}, {"id": "S07", "locator": "determinatives-as-nouns.tex:568", "text": "Target restrictions apply to the nominal being determined or modified, including a nominal headed by an independent determinative. Thus \\mention{the} permits plural \\mention{few} in \\mention{the few}. Determinative-headed phrases also bear number and count properties: \\mention{few} is plural count, while \\mention{some} takes its interpretation from the construction and domain. The modifier \\mention{this} in \\mention{this much} expresses degree; its permission doesn't follow from demonstrative Det selection."}, {"id": "S09", "locator": "determinatives-as-nouns.tex:612", "text": "The dependent conditions distinguish uses before another nominal from independent uses. In Det or internal Mod function before a target, ordinary \\mention{some} and \\mention{few} exclude external determination, partitive complements, and relative postmodifiers within their own phrase. Independent \\mention{some} and \\mention{few} permit selected partitives and relatives; independent \\mention{few} also permits definite determination and adjectival premodification, as in \\mention{the lucky few}. These permissions don't transfer to \\mention{every} or the articles."}]}
